props.title: We've made this jacket since 1971
props.description: The Salmon Bay Parka pattern has changed twice. Here's what changed and why.
props.author: Ballard
paragraphs: The first Salmon Bay Parka was a PVC-coated cotton shell with taped seams and a drawstring hood. It weighed 1.6 kg. The fishing fleet bought it because it didn't leak, and they put up with the weight because the alternative leaked.

The first pattern change was in 1988, when we moved to a nylon shell with a PU membrane. That cut 400 g and added breathability, and it's the point where the jacket stopped being a marine product and started being an outdoor one. The second change was in 2014: we moved the hand pockets up above the harness line and added the two-way zip. Both came from the fleet.
The hood, the storm flap, and the length haven't changed. If we change them, it'll be because someone standing on a deck told us to.
